Action: Conserve high-quality natural/semi-natural habitat; diversify local farm management
Action_PT: Conservar habitat natural/seminatural de alta qualidade; diversificar o manejo local
Response_measured: Wild bee abundance; wild bee richness
Evidence_summary: Bee abundance and richness were higher in diversified/organic fields and landscapes with more high-quality habitat; landscape configuration effects were weak.
Reference: Kennedy et al. (2013). A global quantitative synthesis of local and landscape effects on wild bee pollinators in agroecosystems.
Caveats: Strong support for habitat quality and local diversification; do not interpret connectivity/configuration alone as a guaranteed increase in pollination or yield.

Action: Maintain biodiversity and reduce landscape simplification
Action_PT: Manter a biodiversidade e reduzir a simplificação da paisagem
Evidence_summary: Biodiversity of service-providing organisms mediates ecosystem services and crop-production benefits; landscape simplification is associated with biodiversity-mediated service losses.
Reference: Dainese et al. (2019). A global synthesis reveals biodiversity-mediated benefits for crop production.
Caveats: Broad synthesis across pollination and biological control; effect sizes are context dependent and should not be converted directly into a fixed economic return.

Action: Restore degraded natural or semi-natural habitat
Action_PT: Restaurar habitat natural ou seminatural degradado
Response_measured: Wild bee abundance; wild bee richness
Evidence_summary: Ecological restoration generally benefits wild bee abundance and richness across restoration approaches.
Reference: Tonietto & Larkin (2018). Habitat restoration benefits wild bees: A meta-analysis.
Caveats: The meta-analysis focused on wild bee abundance/richness in restored habitats, not direct crop yield or economic return.

Action: Establish or maintain diverse, persistent floral strips near pollinator-dependent crops
Action_PT: Implantar ou manter faixas floridas diversas e persistentes próximas às culturas dependentes de polinização
Response_measured: Pollination service; pest control; crop yield
Evidence_summary: Pollination effects depended on flowering-plant diversity, age/permanence of strips and distance from plantings; crop-yield effects were not consistently positive.
Reference: Albrecht et al. (2020). The effectiveness of flower strips and hedgerows on pest control, pollination services and crop yield: a quantitative synthesis.
Caveats: Recommend high-quality floral resources, not generic 'plant flowers'. Do not promise yield gains; effectiveness varies with design and spatial context.

Action: Adopt Integrated Pest and Pollinator Management (IPPM)
Action_PT: Adotar Manejo Integrado de Pragas e Polinizadores (IPPM)
Pollinator_group: Honey bees; bumble bees; solitary bees
Evidence_summary: Pollinator health should be integrated into pest-management research and practice, using non-pesticidal options and lower-risk pesticide choices where appropriate.
Reference: Biddinger & Rajotte (2015). Integrated pest and pollinator management—adding a new dimension to an accepted paradigm.
Caveats: Framework supports integration of pest and pollinator management; it does not provide a universal quantitative reduction in pollinator loss.

Action: Use an IPPM decision framework rather than assuming conventional IPM is pollinator-friendly
Action_PT: Usar uma estrutura de decisão IPPM em vez de assumir que o IPM convencional é automaticamente favorável aos polinizadores
Response_measured: Integrated pest control and pollinator protection
Evidence_summary: Provides a systematic framework for jointly delivering pest management and pollinator protection.
Reference: Egan et al. (2020). Delivering Integrated Pest and Pollinator Management (IPPM).
Caveats: Use as a management framework; do not infer a fixed ecological or economic effect size.

Action: Conserve and restore natural/semi-natural ecosystems and reduce agrochemical stress in Brazilian agricultural landscapes
Action_PT: Conservar e restaurar ecossistemas naturais/seminaturais e reduzir o estresse por agroquímicos em paisagens agrícolas brasileiras
Management_module: Habitat conservation; Habitat restoration; Connectivity; Pollinator-friendly pest management
Target_pressure: Deforestation; fragmentation; resource loss; agrochemical stress
Evidence_summary: Brazilian synthesis emphasizes habitat conservation/restoration, connected pollinator-friendly landscapes and reduction of agrochemical stress as policy and management priorities.
Reference: Hipólito et al. (2026). Pollinator-Friendly Policies in Brazil: History and Future Directions.
Caveats: Strong contextual relevance to Brazil; it is a policy/review synthesis rather than a quantitative intervention-effect meta-analysis.
